sections.h2: How fast can you sell a house in Austin, MN?
sections.html:
Speed in Austin depends on the route you pick and on how clean the paperwork is. A cash buyer can close in a matter of weeks, while a listing runs on the buyer's lender and inspection calendar. Austin is the county seat of Mower County, a city of 26,689 people in southeast Minnesota, so most of the paperwork runs through the Mower County offices on First Street NE.

Before any buyer walks through, a seller can shorten the timeline by sorting out four things: the permit history of the house, the property tax status, any city charges tied to the parcel, and whether the lot sits in an area that flooded in the past. The sections below cover each of them with the Austin and Mower County rules in mind.

  • Sell on the open market and wait for financing and appraisal.
  • Sell privately to a neighbor, relative or investor and handle the paperwork yourself.
  • Accept a cash offer from a buyer who takes the house in its current condition.

sections.h2: What kind of city is Austin, and who buys homes here?
sections.html:
Austin is a meatpacking and healthcare town on the Cedar River, and its buyers are mostly local workers, first-time purchasers and investors. The town was platted in the spring of 1856, became a village in 1868 and a city in 1871. It grew around mills on the river, then around the butcher shop George Hormel opened in 1891, which became Hormel Foods.

Hormel is still the largest employer, and the city is known as SPAM Town USA because the corporate headquarters, a SPAM plant and the Spam Museum are all here. The Hormel Institute, a University of Minnesota cancer research center, is also in town. Austin Public Schools (ISD 492) and Riverland Community College are other large employers, and the hospital is part of Mayo Clinic Health System.

Geography matters for a seller as well. Austin is about 41 miles southwest of Rochester, 20 miles east of Albert Lea and 12 miles north of the Iowa line, with Interstate 90 on the east side. Those distances shape who answers a listing here: people tied to the plant, the hospital and the college, plus investors who look at small-town rents.

At $953 a month, median rent is low as well, which is why some Austin owners keep a house as a rental and others decide to sell it. If you are weighing that choice, the rental registration rules below are worth reading first.

sections.h2: Does a flood history affect selling a house in Austin?
sections.html:
Yes, it can, because many Austin homes were built in the Cedar River floodplain and buyers and lenders ask about it. The city's flood history lists major floods in July 1978, 1983, 1993, spring 2000 when the Cedar River crested at 23.4 feet, September 2004 and 2010. Dobbins Creek and Turtle Creek also run through town.

The city answered with buyouts. Flood-prone homes were purchased and demolished using a Community Development Block Grant and the Hazard Mitigation Grant Program, low areas were turned into parks, dikes were added after 2004, and a flood wall protecting downtown was finished in 2014. If your house is near the river or one of the creeks, ask City Hall at 500 4th Avenue NE for the parcel's floodplain status before you list, and ask your insurance agent what flood coverage costs.

Tornadoes are the other weather risk on record. An EF2 tornado crossed the northwest and north side of Austin on June 17, 2009. Roof age, siding and tree condition are the details a buyer's inspector will notice after a storm-prone stretch of years.

sections.h2: What permit and yard rules should an Austin seller check first?
sections.html:
Check your permit record first. The city's own FAQ warns that if you sell a building with modifications done without a permit, you may be required to tear the addition down, leave it unoccupied or pay for costly repairs. Permits are usually needed for additions, decks, garages, fences, pools, water heaters, re-roofing and electrical, plumbing and heating work.

Two routine ordinances also generate liens against sellers who ignore them.

  • Grass and weeds. City Code 10.13 sets an 8 inch height limit. After a notice from the weed inspector you have seven days to comply, then the city cuts it and certifies the cost to the Mower County Auditor as a special assessment collected like real estate taxes.
  • Sidewalk snow. Chapter 7.04 requires owners to clear public sidewalks within 12 hours after snow stops, and the city may clear them after 24 hours and bill the owner.

Deal with both before closing, since an unpaid assessment is collected the way real estate taxes are. Austin also does not allow chickens, which matters if you kept hens and a buyer asks about the coop.

sections.h2: Do Austin rental registration rules apply when you sell?
sections.html:
They apply if the house is a rental, and they can affect the buyer. Austin requires residential rental property to be registered under City Ordinance 4.29, and the city's rental program FAQ says a Change of Ownership form must be filed when a rental is sold. Ask the city whether the same tenants will stay with the new owner, because that decides which form is used.

If you live elsewhere for part of the year, the program also asks you to name a local rental manager who handles emergencies and inspections. A buyer who plans to keep the tenants will want to see the rental registration and any inspection results, so pull those documents together before you accept an offer.

sections.h2: How do Mower County property taxes work at closing?
sections.html:
Mower County bills property tax in two halves, due May 15 and October 15, and second-half agricultural tax is due November 15. The Auditor-Treasurer's office is in the Government Center at 201 First Street NE, Suite 7, in Austin, and the phone is 507-437-9535.

  • The county does not mail second-half statements, so a buyer should ask for the amount.
  • Mail payments are judged by postmark, and a private postage meter mark does not count.
  • The county will not accept post-dated checks.
  • A missing statement does not excuse a late payment.

On the deed side, Minnesota Statute 287.21 sets the state deed tax at .0033 of the net consideration when the price is above $3,000, and the Hennepin County recorder's checklist adds that an eCRV is required for sales over $3,000 and that a deed cannot pass title while taxes are delinquent. A well statement or well disclosure certificate also has to accompany a transfer deed. Ask the Mower County recorder for the local filing steps and fees.

sections.h2: What must you tell a buyer in writing?
sections.html:
Minnesota Statute 513.55 requires a written disclosure of material facts you know before the purchase agreement is signed. It covers facts that could adversely and significantly affect an ordinary buyer's use and enjoyment of the property, made in good faith and to the best of your knowledge. A separate radon statute, section 144.496, adds a written radon disclosure and a copy of the Minnesota Department of Health booklet.

For an Austin house, the facts buyers care about most are basement water, past flooding, roof and furnace age, and any work done without a permit. Writing these down early keeps negotiations short, and it matters even more in a quick sale where the buyer is not hiring an inspector.

faqs.q: Do I need an inspection from the city before selling in Austin?
faqs.a: Ask the building department at City Hall, 500 4th Avenue NE, whether any sale-time step applies to your address, and gather your permits and any rental registration so a buyer can see them.

faqs.q: What happens if I have unpermitted work on my Austin house?
faqs.a: A buyer may be able to require you to remove it, leave it unoccupied or pay for repairs. The city's FAQ says exactly that about modifications made without a permit, so ask the building office whether the work can be permitted after the fact before you list.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in Mower County?
faqs.a: May 15 and October 15, with second-half agricultural tax due November 15. The county does not mail second-half statements, so request the figure from the Auditor-Treasurer at 507-437-9535 if you need it for closing.

faqs.q: Can a high weed or grass notice block my sale?
faqs.a: It will not block the sale by itself, but unpaid mowing costs become a special assessment on the parcel. Austin allows 8 inches of grass and gives seven days after notice, so cut it early and ask the clerk for any pending charges.

faqs.q: Is Austin a good place to sell to a landlord or investor?
faqs.a: Often yes. Median rent is $953 and 71.5 percent of homes are owner-occupied, so investors look at the town. Registered rentals must follow Austin's rental ordinance, and a sold rental needs a Change of Ownership form filed with the city.
